pairs.subject: offer-lifecycle-and-deadlines
pairs.evidence: app/offer/[token]/OfferClient.tsx:17 The page does tell an expired link apart from an invalid one (404 card vs expired card), but the lapsed answer carries only the role and never the date and time the offer expired, and the 410 on a late accept is a bare refusal with no recorded attempt routed to a recruiter, so the 'known but lapsed' answer the technique requires is incomplete.

techniques.evidence: app/offer/[token]/kit/OfferKitView.tsx:112 Distinct from the 404 invalidLink card (OfferClient.tsx:92) and the role is still named in the letter head, but expiredBody ('The deadline to respond has passed…') states no expiry date/time because offerView strips expiresAt; the technique says the lapsed answer must say 'this offer for this role expired on this date and time'. Separately, respondToOffer (app/_lib/offer-finalize.ts:35-36) returns OFFER_EXPIRED without recording the post-deadline attempt as an event for a recruiter.

app/offer/[token]/kit/offerKitModel.ts:69 Authority holds: hours/minutes are computed on the server and rounded up (offer-policy.ts offerHoursRemaining uses Math.ceil), the page re-fetches on focus/visibility and every 60s (OfferClient.tsx:171), the absolute deadline is shown in a named zone, and decline goes through an inline confirm. But units are not chosen by proximity: anything over an hour is shown in hours, so a 7-day offer reads '168 hours left' where the technique wants days, and the countdown is always shown rather than only in the last stretch.

app/offer/[token]/offer-response.ts:36 The client settles any 2xx that names a recorded outcome, so the server's CAS-loser reply (ok:true, alreadyResponded, from markOfferResponded's `WHERE status = 'extended'` UPDATE in offers-store.ts) renders as success instead of an error. Only one response can be in flight at a time, an ambiguous POST triggers a re-read of the authoritative state, and lapse is checked before accept on the server.
